title: Work IQ: federated connectors for governed access to more data sources
summary: The roadmap details, licensing, default connector access and documented governance controls are supported. The action rating should be act-now rather than review: existing configured connectors participate automatically, and the roadmap target is this month.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans federated connectors for governed Work IQ access to additional enterprise data sources.
claims.quote: Enable Work IQ to use federated connectors for governed access to additional enterprise data sources.

claims.claim: The listed products are Microsoft Graph and Work IQ.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Graph", "Work IQ"]

claims.claim: The roadmap status remains In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is November CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview target is October CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "October CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists the Developer platform.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Developer"]

claims.claim: Connector access in Work IQ is enabled by default, corresponding to defaultState on.
claims.quote: Connector access is enabled by default.

claims.claim: Connector participation requires that the connector be available to the signed-in user.
claims.quote: Copilot Connectors, both synced and federated, participate in Work IQ APIs when they're available to the signed-in user and connected by that user as data sources in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Connector participation requires that the user connect the source in Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: Copilot Connectors, both synced and federated, participate in Work IQ APIs when they're available to the signed-in user and connected by that user as data sources in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Work IQ must be enabled for the organisation.
claims.quote: Prerequisites: Enable Work IQ for your organization.

claims.claim: Configured Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors automatically participate in Work IQ APIs, subject to the stated conditions.
claims.quote: Copilot Connectors configured in Microsoft 365 Copilot automatically participate in Work IQ APIs.

claims.claim: Data sensitivity requirements or partner agreements may limit connector participation.
claims.quote: Not every Copilot Connector configured in Microsoft 365 Copilot is available through Work IQ. Connector participation might be limited by data sensitivity requirements or partner agreements.

claims.claim: Learn describes connected enterprise sources participating in Work IQ Copilot, entity and schema tools.
claims.quote: Connected enterprise sources participate in Work IQ Copilot, entity, and schema tools.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Federated connectors use Model Context Protocol to fetch external data in real time.
claims.quote: Use Model Context Protocol (MCP) to fetch data in real time.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Federated connector access uses the user's identity and permissions.
claims.quote: Access data using the user's identity and permissions.

claims.claim: Federated connectors do not index external data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Don't index external data into Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Administrators manage federated connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Are managed and governed by admins in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The source system enforces permissions for federated connector access.
claims.quote: The source system enforces all permissions. Users can only access content they're authorized to view and make changes they're authorized to make in the original data source.

claims.claim: Federated connectors do not copy the source data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Federated connectors don't copy or store data in Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Live external data is retrieved into Copilot responses.
claims.quote: Copilot selects relevant connector tools at runtime and uses the live results returned by the source to respond in the conversation.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot can create, update or delete source data where a connector provides those tools.
claims.quote: Where a connector provides the tools, Copilot can also create, update, or delete data in the connected system on the user's behalf.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: Connector write tools initially require user approval.
claims.quote: Tools that create, update, or delete data initially require the user's explicit approval. Users can choose whether Copilot asks again for that tool, as described in Confirm an action.

claims.claim: New write-capable connector tools default to Needs approval.
claims.quote: If a connector publisher adds a new write-capable tool or changes an existing one, the tool is set to Needs approval by default.

claims.claim: Federated connectors remain read-only in the Researcher agent.
claims.quote: The Researcher agent doesn't support write, update, or delete actions. Federated Copilot connectors remain read-only in this experience.

claims.claim: The general connectors overview still describes federated connectors as read-only, unlike the federated overview's write-action documentation.
claims.quote: Federated connectors are read-only; they can search and fetch content but can't write data back.

claims.claim: MCP server firewalls may require static egress IP allow-listing.
claims.quote: If your MCP server restricts incoming traffic by source IP address, configure its firewall to allow the static egress IP addresses used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: Federated Copilot connector users require a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence or Microsoft 365 E7.
claims.quote: Federated Copilot connectors are available only to tenants and users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license (or Microsoft 365 E7).

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing.
claims.quote: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Work IQ API uses usage-based billing, corresponding to the consumption licensing model.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.where: front matter: cost; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits, supporting the variable cost rating.
claims.quote: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.

claims.claim: Work IQ's Copilot Credits are shared with other eligible services.
claims.quote: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.

claims.claim: The Foundry Work IQ page is preview documentation.
claims.quote: Connect agents to Microsoft 365 with Work IQ (preview)

claims.claim: The Foundry page distinguishes A2A, REST and MCP Work IQ API billing from connector licensing.
claims.quote: Work IQ API through A2A, REST, or MCP | Usage-based billing | Enable billing with Copilot Credits. This path doesn't use connector licensing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Connector-backed Microsoft 365 tools have connector-specific licensing requirements that must be checked.
claims.quote: Connector-backed Microsoft 365 tools | Connector licensing | Confirm the selected connector's prerequisites. A connector can require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license for each calling user.

claims.claim: Existing Microsoft 365 admin-center connector allow and block controls apply through Work IQ APIs.
claims.quote: Existing administrator controls in the Microsoft 365 admin center to allow or block Copilot Connectors also apply when Connectors are accessed through Work IQ APIs.

claims.claim: Individual connector enable, disable and staged-rollout settings are reached in Microsoft 365 admin center through Copilot > Connectors > Your connections > connector.
claims.quote: Enable / Disable | Copilot > Connectors > Your connections | Turns an individual connector on or pauses it without removing configuration. Staged rollout | Copilot > Connectors > Your connections > Staged rollout

claims.where: controls[0].api; rendered controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/unblock allows a blocked Copilot package to be used.
claims.quote: Unblock a Copilot package to allow its usage. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/unblock

claims.claim: Blocking a federated connector has the same effect as disabling it.
claims.quote: Block (Agents > Tools) has the same effect as Disable.

claims.claim: Package Management block and unblock calls require a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: Block and unblock require the delegated CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All permission.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All | Not available.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not support these beta APIs in production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Package block and unblock calls do not configure staged rollout.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. Request body: Don't supply a request body for this method.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no automation for federated connector staged rollout at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: federated connector staged rollout Microsoft Graph copilotPackage API users groups PowerShell; "federated" "staged rollout" "API". Read connector management, custom connector, Package Management overview and staged-rollout excerpts; no staging call.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access controls connector availability by publisher type.
claims.quote: Admins control which federated connectors are available in their organization from Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: controls[1].api; rendered controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors with mode applyOnce applies the publisher-type baseline once.
claims.quote: Create a new configurationMonitor object that runs periodically in the background at a scheduled frequency to detect configuration drift in monitorOnly mode, or applies a desired-state baseline once in applyOnce mode.

claims.claim: The publisher-type baseline uses microsoft.agent.allowedagenttypes and valueObject properties areMicrosoftAppsAllowed, areTenantScopedAppsAllowed and areISVAppsAllowed.
claims.quote: "resourceType": "microsoft.agent.allowedagenttypes", "resourceVersion": 1, "properties": { "valueObject": { "areMicrosoftAppsAllowed": true, "areTenantScopedAppsAllowed": true, "areISVAppsAllowed": false, "areMicrosoftCertifiedThirdPartyAppsAllowed": true } }

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access controls who can use connectors.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins. Plugins include tools, MCP servers, connectors, skills, and other AI artifacts.

claims.where: controls[2].api; rendered controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors with mode applyOnce applies the User access baseline once.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors. An active applyOnce monitor runs in the background on behalf of the signed-in administrator and then becomes inactive.

claims.claim: microsoft.agent.useraccess uses valueObject.userAssignmentCategory with everyone or noOne, rather than specific-group assignment.
claims.quote: AgentUserAccessValueObject: userAssignmentCategory | Write | String | Specifies whether all users or no users can access agents and plugins. | everyone, noOne

claims.claim: The signed-in user needs the AI Administrator role for Agent resource applyOnce operations.
claims.quote: AI Administrator is the least-privileged role for the signed-in user for remediation and applyOnce; don't assign that user-role requirement to the service principal.

claims.claim: The app calling applyOnce needs delegated ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote: Creating an applyOnce monitor supports delegated permissions only. In addition to the calling app's delegated ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All permission, the TCM service principal needs delegated permissions for the target workloads.

claims.claim: The TCM service principal needs delegated CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite for these Agent resource operations.
claims.quote: For remediation and applyOnce, grant it the CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite delegated permission.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP tenant policy settings are reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools. In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP. On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: An API for the Work IQ MCP tenant policy toggle is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP tenant policy enable disable Graph API PowerShell; Work IQ policy copilotPackage API Allowed Disallowed; Work IQ MCP policy configurationManagement API. Read policy-governance-mcp, Agent TCM resources and Package Management overview; no toggle call.

claims.claim: Tenant policy can explicitly enable or disable connector participation in Work IQ paths.
claims.quote: Administrators can explicitly enable or disable connector participation in Work IQ paths through tenant-level policies.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP details pane exposes the Policy tab when it is available.
claims.quote: On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy changes can take up to 24 hours to apply across the tenant.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.claim: Federated connector activity can be audited in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Can read data and, where a connector provides the tools, create, update, or delete data with the user's approval. Admins can audit activity in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: Always allow applies to an individual connector tool, not the whole connector.
claims.quote: Always allow and Allow for conversation apply to the individual tool, not to the whole connector. Users can decide which tools to allow.

claims.claim: Allow for conversation applies to an individual connector tool, not the whole connector.
claims.quote: Always allow and Allow for conversation apply to the individual tool, not to the whole connector. Users can decide which tools to allow.

claims.claim: The review action rating fits this change.
claims.quote: action: "review"; defaultState: "on"; targetDate: "November CY2026"; risk: "medium"; Copilot Connectors configured in Microsoft 365 Copilot automatically participate in Work IQ APIs.
claims.fix: Set action to act-now. On the 21 November 2026 run, the November target is within about 60 days, connector access is enabled by default for existing eligible connected sources, risk is medium, and documented connector and tenant-policy controls allow an administrator to decide access before it lands.

claims.claim: Tenant Configuration Management applyOnce support for these Agent resources is in preview.
claims.quote: Tenant Configuration Management (TCM) drift remediation and applyOnce monitors change workload configuration on behalf of the signed-in administrator. These capabilities are available in preview through Microsoft Graph beta.
